claims.claim_summary: The paper identifies a selection mismatch between magnitude ranking and attention matrix multiplication
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We identify a long-standing selection mismatch in sparse attention: existing magnitude-based rules approximate the attention matrix entrywise, while the Transformer uses attention through matrix multiplication.

evidence_spans.source_text: Therefore, current sparse selection asks which entries or regions of A are large. It does not ask which selected entries best preserve the actual attention output AV.
This shows that entrywise magnitude ranking is correct only when V V ⊤behaves like an identity matrix over token positions. This condition does not hold in long-context attention.
